newsitem.title: UK: Britain calls for wide popular EU debate on future.
newsitem.headline: Britain calls for wide popular EU debate on future.

text.p: Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind on Thursday called for a "much wider popular debate" across the European Union on its future shape, insisting most bloc citizens reject a federal superstate.
In a keynote speech, he rejected the notion that decisions should be taken by diplomats and politicians without regard to the views of ordinary people.
"In the new modern Europe the debate must no longer be reserved to the political class, but involve the whole adult population," he told London's French Chamber of Commerce.
Rifkind said most Europeans did not want Brussels to be given new powers unless it was unavoidable.
"Most people still expect that decisions affecting them should be taken by their politicians, speaking their language, who are accountable to them," Rifkind said.
Eurosceptic Conservatives fear the EU is heading for a centralised structure which would make its constituent countries mere regions of a government administered in Brussels.
But Rifkind insisted there was a third way between a federal Europe and a mere trading bloc of the sort these Eurosceptics seek.

"Britain's view is that the best future for us all lies in a Partnership of Nations, where Europe concentrates single-mindedly on what needs to be done at a European level, and does it well," he said.
He said the ideal that supranational measures should be kept to a minimum was as relevant to ordinary people in France, Germany or Italy as it was to Britons.

"Tens of millions of people throughout Europe are as determined as we are to build a Europe based on cooperation and partnership, but are also, like us, uneasy and unimpressed by the desire to supplant the nation state," he said.

Rifkind's speech was the first of a series he plans across Europe to put forward Britain's views on the future of Europe ahead of a summit meeting in Amsterdam in June which is due to make key decisions on the bloc's future.
